title: Petra and the Witness
premise: Retired detective Bram Sandoval is paid a suspiciously large retainer by a nervous woman named Petra to prove that a murder has not yet happened — a murder the client insists is fated, foretold by entries in an old shipping ledger. As Bram investigates the ledger's coded accounts, she discovers it records not cargo but debts of silence: payments made to witnesses who agreed to forget a drowning twenty years ago in the harbor town of Saltmere. When Petra disappears and the first 'predicted' victim turns up dead exactly as the ledger foretold, Bram realizes her client was never asking her to prevent a murder — she was asking Bram to witness one before becoming its next entry. In the climax, Bram decodes the final page at the tide flats where the original body was hidden, confronting the killer — Saltmere's beloved harbormaster — and choosing truth over the comfortable lie that kept the town whole.
about_author: Felix Almeida is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers from forgotten coastal towns. They write mysteries about paper trails that outlive the people who left them.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Bram Sandoval, retired detective turned failing bookseller, takes a strange case: Petra Voss pays triple rate to prove a murder hasn't happened yet, sliding a photocopied ledger page across the counter. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking the ache of irrelevance — Bram can't afford to refuse, and knows it.

chapters.title: The Ledger That Counts Backward
chapters.summary: Bram studies the ledger, finding dates listed for deaths that haven't occurred, including one three days out bearing Petra's own name. She traces the book to Saltmere's defunct cannery office. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: creeping dread as professional skepticism collides with evidence she can't explain away.

chapters.title: Saltmere Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: In Saltmere, everyone Bram interviews is warm, helpful, and identically vague about the summer a cannery worker drowned. The harbormaster, Edom Hale, charms her over chowder. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: unease beneath small-town hospitality — a town rehearsed in forgetting.

chapters.title: Petra's Second Story
chapters.summary: Bram catches Petra in a lie about her connection to Saltmere; confronted, Petra admits she's the drowned worker's daughter, raised on a deathbed confession that the drowning was no accident. POV: Bram, with Petra's account in dialogue. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into reluctant empathy.

chapters.title: Debits of Silence
chapters.summary: Bram cracks the code: the ledger's 'payments' are hush money to five witnesses, each entry initialed E.H. One witness, still living, is scheduled to die in two days. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grim triumph turning cold — decoding the past means predicting the next killing.

chapters.title: The Tide Takes the First One
chapters.summary: Bram races to protect the surviving witness, arrives too late: he's dead on the tide flats, arranged precisely as the ledger described. Police call it an accident. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: guilt and fury — she treated this as a puzzle when it was a countdown.

chapters.title: What Petra Bought
chapters.summary: Digging into Petra's finances, Bram finds the retainer came from hush-money funds Petra inherited — she bought Bram's investigation with blood money. Then Petra vanishes. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: disillusionment; loyalty to a client who may have been running her all along.

chapters.title: Edom's Honest Face
chapters.summary: Bram confronts Hale with the ledger; he confesses to the cover-up but swears the drownings since are coincidence or Petra's doing, offering her a place in the town's quiet. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: temptation — the price of survival is a lie she could almost live with.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Following tide charts and the ledger's final coded coordinates, Bram finds Petra bound in the cannery boathouse as Hale arrives to close the last open account. A violent confrontation on the flooding flats. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve — witness becomes participant.

chapters.title: What the Water Gives Back
chapters.summary: Hale is arrested when the original victim's remains surface with the spring tide, corroborating everything. Petra, complicit in manipulating Bram, leaves without forgiveness sought or given. Bram reopens the bookshop, ledger donated to the archive. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: hard-won peace — truth cost everything except itself.
